title: Client KPI Lab Notebook — latency, cost/token, cache hit
content:
Purpose and context

This is a working lab notebook for building a compact, repeatable QBR metrics sheet focused on the four operational signals we keep seeing drive renewal conversations: latency, uptime (availability), cost per token, and cache hit rate. The goal: a single page definition + calculation canonical that CS can generate for each customer ahead of a quarterly review, plus a small risk mapping that converts metric deltas into renewal conversation prompts (not canned playbooks).

Audience
- Customer Success leads preparing QBRs
- Solutions engineers who validate instrumentation
- Product managers & SREs for data accuracy and measurement alignment

High-level guidance (short)
1) Use the same raw sources we use in Console: per-request timing traces + per-route token accounting + cache events exported to the warehouse.
2) Compute rolling 7d and 90d baselines; present both in the QBR.
3) Prefer percent-change and absolute delta side-by-side. Customers understand both.
4) Annotate spikes with incident ids and PRs where applicable.

Metric definitions and canonical formulas (single-line each)
1) Median latency (P50) — definition: median server-side time between request start and first response byte for generation/chat routes.
   Formula: P50_latency = median(request_end_time - request_start_time) over chosen window (exclude synthetic probes).
   Notes: use server-side timestamps to avoid client clock skew; exclude requests with status != 200.

2) Tail latency (P95) — definition: 95th percentile of server-side end-to-end latency for the route.
   Formula: P95_latency = 95th_percentile(request_end_time - request_start_time).
   Notes: call out large-seq requests separately. If >5% of traffic is long-context ( > 2k tokens), report a split.

3) Uptime / availability (SLA-style) — definition: percentage of successful requests (returning 2xx) weighted by time or by request count depending on contract.
   Formula: availability = 100 * (successful_requests / total_requests) in the window.
   Notes: for dedicated customers with SLA, use weighted-by-request; for low-volume customers we show raw count and #downtime-minutes with incident refs.

4) Cost per token (unit econ) — definition: total server-side compute cost attributed to customer divided by total tokens generated (input + output) in window.
   Formula: cost_per_token = (sum(compute_seconds * instance_cost_rate) + cache_miss_cost_adjustments) / sum(tokens).
   Notes: We currently approximate compute_seconds via per-request GPU-seconds; highlight if estimated (and how). Show both platform-calculated cost_per_token and invoice-aligned cost where available.

5) Cache hit rate — definition: percentage of requests where token generation used a valid cache prefix / KV cache hit that avoided full generation work.
   Formula: cache_hit_rate = 100 * (cache_hits / cache_lookups).
   Notes: normalize lookups to generation attempts (exclude purely embedding-only requests). Break down hits by prefix length band (short/medium/long).

Measurement sources (practical)
- Traces table (warehouse): request_id, route, start_ts, end_ts, status, seq_len_est, downstream_errors.
- Token ledger: request_id -> input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens.
- Cost attribution table: instance_id, gpu_seconds, customer_id, rate (USD / gpu-second).
- Cache events: request_id, cache_lookup, cache_hit_boolean, prefix_tokens_saved.

Calculation rules & sanity checks
- Always present raw counts next to ratios (e.g., 13k requests, 98.4% availability).
- If sample size < 100 requests in window, mark metric as low-confidence and show raw count.
- For P95, if distribution is multimodal, include a histogram snippet or bucketed percentiles (P50/75/90/95/99).
- Cost per token should be shown both as per-1k tokens and per-token to align with different reading habits.

Thresholds and suggested triggers (starter playbook)
- Latency P95 increase > 25% vs 90d baseline -> cause: model variant change, infra regression, larger sequences. Action: add to agenda; ask SE to validate kernel selection and batch sizing.
- Availability drop > 0.5 percentage points and > 1 hour impact -> open incident review and check routing fallback config.
- Cost/token up > 30% -> ask for query mix (longer prompts, more streaming), show Optimize suggestions (quantization, batching, routing).
- Cache hit rate drop of >10 percentage points with stable traffic -> check cache invalidation rules and prompt engineering changes.

KPI table template (one-line headers; meant for export into sheet)
Row headers: metric | window | raw_count | baseline | current_value | delta_abs | delta_pct | confidence | notes
Example rows (sample numbers)
- Median latency | 7d | 12,432 req | baseline 120 ms | current 140 ms | +20 ms | +16.7% | high | increased after model v2 rollout (PR #456)
- P95 latency | 7d | 12,432 req | baseline 350 ms | current 460 ms | +110 ms | +31% | med | long-seq traffic up 6%
- Availability | 30d | 1,234,567 req | baseline 99.92% | current 99.78% | -0.14 ppt | -0.14% | high | 2 incidents (INC-778, INC-779)
- Cost per 1k tokens | 30d | 1.2M tokens | baseline $1.10 | current $1.52 | +$0.42 | +38% | med | change in model family + no quantization
- Cache hit rate | 7d | 11,890 lookups | baseline 62% | current 52% | -10 ppt | -16% | med | template changes upstream

Renewal signal mapping (quick, human): how to phrase in QBR
- Low-risk: all metrics within ±10% of baseline; present as health ok and focus on feature adoption.
- Moderate-risk: one metric outside threshold (latency or cost) -> propose Optimize workshop (cost reduction + QoE tradeoffs).
- Elevated-risk: two or more metrics outside thresholds OR availability < SLA threshold for > 1 week -> schedule escalation and SE-led remediation plan.

Examples of short narrative snippets to use in QBR slides
- "Performance: P95 latency increased 31% versus 90-day baseline after model v2 rollout; sequence-length distribution shifted +6% long-context. SE investigating continuous-batching tuning and kernel selection."
- "Cost: cost per 1k tokens increased 38% month-over-month driven by model mix; suggested mitigations: enable 8-bit quantization for non-critical routes and enable prefix cache for high-reuse flows."

Open questions / research items (notes to self)
- How to reconcile platform cost_per_token with finance invoice lines (mapping table exists but edge cases where multi-tenant hosts split GPU cost need validation).
- Should cache hit rate be weighted by tokens saved instead of lookup count? (proposal: show both).
- Investigate an automated pre-QBR diagnostic that alerts when a metric crosses thresholds and auto-generates context (incidents, PRs, top callers).

Quick checklist for CS lead before QBR
- [ ] Pull 7d and 90d windows for the defined metrics.
- [ ] Validate trace-to-token join for sample of 50 requests.
- [ ] Add incident/PR annotations to any metric with >15% delta.
- [ ] Write 2-3 bulleted customer-facing action items (Optimize suggestions + quick wins).

Appendix: abbreviated example SQL snippets (high-level, for SE use)
- P95 latency: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (end_ts-start_ts)) FROM traces WHERE route = 'generation' AND start_ts BETWEEN X AND Y;
- Cache hit rate: SELECT 100.0*sum(case when cache_hit then 1 else 0 end)/count(*) FROM cache_events WHERE start_ts BETWEEN X AND Y;

End of lab notebook — save as a template and iterate.

Notes: keep this intentionally lightweight — CS decks need single-page clarity. This doc will evolve with instrumentation improvements and Optimize feature rollout.
